findings.claim: Option C's explanation (and need 3 at line 388) says a TreeMap<String, Integer> prints customers 'alphabetically'. TreeMap orders String keys by their natural ordering, which String.compareTo defines as lexicographic by Unicode (UTF-16) value: case-sensitive, so 'ana' sorts after 'Ben'. 'Alphabetical' is accurate only when names share capitalization, as they do in this scenario. Not a wrong answer, but an imprecise general statement in a recap-style cost/order claim.

evidence.section: Class description: 'sorted according to the natural ordering of its keys, or by a Comparator provided at map creation time'
compareTo(String): 'The comparison is based on the Unicode value of each character in the strings ... compared lexicographically'

findings.recommendation: Say 'sorted by name (String natural ordering)' or add 'for consistently capitalized names' once, e.g. in option C's explanation or the recap line 'a TreeMap keeps keys sorted'. Optional: mention String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER as the comparator for a case-blind report.
